reason: The cited evidence (all from the same paper) directly demonstrates training a deep neural network potential for (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x, using hysteresis and two-phase methods to predict melting temperature with ±30 K error, and explains the nonlinear composition trend with nitrogen. However, the evidence only covers melting temperature and structural analysis; it does not report predictions of enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, or volume change at melting, leaving those premises unsupported.
premises: Deep neural network potentials can be trained on ab initio MD to describe solid and liquid states of high-entropy carbonitrides.
Such potentials enable accurate prediction of melting temperature via hysteresis and two-phase coexistence methods.
The approach can capture composition-dependent trends in melting temperature, enthalpy, entropy, and volume change.
Nitrogen content systematically increases melting temperature in (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x, with a maximum near 25% N.
The method is computationally efficient enough to screen compositions within the high-entropy alloy family.
